newsitem.title: UK: British core inflation 2.7 percent in March.
newsitem.headline: British core inflation 2.7 percent in March.

text.p: British core inflation rose by 0.3 percent in March, bringing the annual rate to 2.7 percent, the Office for National Statistics said on Thursday.
The figures were better than expected by economic analysts and would provide a boost for the ruling Conservative Party ahead of the May 1 election.
The monthly inflation rate in February was 0.4 percent, with core annual inflation standing at 2.9 percent.

The core inflation rate excludes mortgage payments and the government had been hoping to reduce the figure to 2.5 percent by the end of the current parliament. Analysts said that although the target had been missed, an outcome of 2.7 percent would please the government.

Jeremy Hawkins of Bank of America said: "The government must be pretty pleased with today's numbers. They will use today's numbers, together with a strong employment report yesterday, to underline the generally strong performance we're seeing in the UK economy."
Prime Minister John Major said Britain was enjoying the "longest period of low inflation for 50 years and I expect that to continue".
